title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Dow jumped 530 pts (+1%) Monday, S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq flat, as hopes of revived U.S.-Iran diplomacy talks sparked an afternoon rebound; Asian markets slid overnight after S. Korean data-center IPO Elice crashed 32% on its debut, dragging the Kospi down 3.7%.
Markets: Oil slipped — Brent -0.7% to $108.79/bbl, WTI -1.8% to $101.79/bbl; 10-year Treasury yield ~5.12%.
Companies: GM shares fell 6.8% (worst in the S&P 500) after narrowing 2027 guidance and warning of a rocky year ahead, even as it announced a fresh $20B buyback.
Companies: Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus shows explosive revenue growth alongside a net loss of more than $80B in H1 2026 and risks tied to a narrow customer base.
Companies: CoreWeave shares and bonds remain under pressure (down roughly a third in a month); WSJ argues Nvidia, which owns ~10% of CoreWeave, has strong incentive to backstop it if trouble deepens.

Macro/Policy: Goldman Sachs warns power, not chips, is now the biggest risk to the AI buildout — data-center electricity demand is seen surging 170% by 2030, requiring ~$7.6T in capex through 2031; grid-connection queues average ~5 years.
Macro/Policy: Elon Musk pledged to give every U.S. child one SpaceX share (~$10B total) next year, joining other AI-boom leaders sharing wealth via new 'Trump Accounts.'
